title: Best Shower Heads UK
short: Eight shower heads tested on both a high-flow mixer shower and a lower-flow electric shower, checking every spray pattern with shower gel and shampoo, from £7.99 to £103.
intro: A shower head that's brilliant on a powerful mixer shower can be disappointing on a low-pressure electric one, so testing across both matters. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup (8 April 2024), where testers fitted each head to a high-flow mixer shower with a booster pump and a lower-flow electric shower, tried every spray pattern using shower gel and shampoo to judge cleaning and hair-rinsing performance, assessed how comfortable any soft spray or massage patterns felt, and measured flow rate in litres per minute for any head claiming water-saving credentials.

products.name: Harmony
products.best_for: Buyers with decent water pressure who want the best all-round performance
products.key_spec: 105mm head, 4 spray patterns, works on mixer or power showers, anti-kink thread
products.summary: Expert Reviews' top overall pick, impressing with excellent build quality and an anti-kink thread that keeps the hose tangle-free. It performed strongly across all four spray patterns in testing, though it needs decent water pressure behind it to show its best, so it's less suited to a weak electric shower.
pros: Strong performance across all spray patterns
cons: Needs decent water pressure to perform at its best

products.name: Complento G804
products.best_for: Buyers on electric showers who want strong performance for very little money
products.key_spec: 100mm head, 5 spray patterns, works on all shower types, 5-year warranty
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this gave good results specifically on electric showers, unusual for such a cheap head, with five spray patterns to choose from and a 5-year warranty that outlasts pricier rivals. It's the standout value pick of the group.
pros: Performs well even on weaker electric showers
cons: Build feels basic next to premium options

products.name: 7000 Series
products.best_for: Buyers who want lots of spray pattern choice without spending much
products.key_spec: 110mm head, 5 spray patterns, works on all shower types
products.summary: Expert Reviews rated this a budget-friendly all-rounder, offering five spray patterns that work across mixer, power and electric showers alike. It doesn't have the premium finish of the pricier heads on test, and its warranty is shorter at one year, but it covers most household needs at a low price.
pros: Five spray patterns for the price
Works well across all shower types

products.name: Satinjet Kiri
products.best_for: Buyers who want a gentle, spa-like rainfall spray
products.key_spec: 106mm head, single spray pattern, 8L/min flow rate (measured)
products.summary: Expert Reviews measured an 8 litre-per-minute flow rate on this single-pattern rainfall head, delivering a gentle spray that testers found relaxing rather than powerful. It's a good match if a soft, enveloping shower matters more to you than raw pressure.
pros: Good value for a rainfall-style head
cons: Only one spray pattern, no versatility

products.name: Aurajet AIO
products.best_for: Buyers who want to cut water use without sacrificing feel
products.key_spec: 132mm ring design, single spray pattern, 9L/min flow rate (measured)
products.summary: Expert Reviews measured a 9 litre-per-minute flow rate, a genuine water saving over higher-flow heads on test, without the spray feeling noticeably weaker. Its distinctive ring design stands out visually, backed by a 5-year warranty.
pros: Measured water saving without weak spray feel

products.name: Raindance Select S 150
products.best_for: Buyers with strong water pressure who want a premium, powerful shower
products.key_spec: 150mm head, 3 spray patterns including rotating massage jets, high pressure
products.summary: Expert Reviews' premium pick, with a large 150mm head, three spray patterns including rotating massage jets, and a genuinely high-end feel and finish. It's the most expensive head on test, and needs strong pressure behind it, but delivers the most powerful, spa-like experience of the group.
cons: Needs strong water pressure to perform well

guide.q: Will any shower head work on my electric shower?
guide.a: No. Expert Reviews specifically tested each head on both a high-flow mixer shower and a lower-flow electric shower, and found performance varies a lot between the two. The Grifema Complento G804 stood out for working well even on a weaker electric shower, while some higher-pressure heads like the Aqualisa Harmony need stronger flow to perform at their best.

guide.q: How many spray patterns do I actually need?
guide.a: Expert Reviews tested heads with anywhere from one pattern up to five. A single-pattern head like the Methven Satinjet Kiri suits buyers who know exactly what shower feel they want, while a multi-pattern head like the Triton 7000 Series or Grifema gives more flexibility for different household members.

guide.q: Do water-saving shower heads actually save water?
guide.a: Expert Reviews measured real flow rates rather than relying on manufacturer claims: the Methven Aurajet AIO measured 9L/min and the Satinjet Kiri 8L/min, both genuine reductions compared with a typical unrestricted flow, without the testers finding the spray felt noticeably weaker.

guide.q: Is it worth paying for a premium head like the Hansgrohe?
guide.a: If your home has strong water pressure, Expert Reviews found the Hansgrohe Raindance Select S 150 delivered the most powerful, premium-feeling shower on test, including rotating massage jets. On weaker pressure or an electric shower, that extra power may go to waste, so a cheaper head like the Aqualisa or Grifema is the better match.
